differences.title: 1. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: NestJS enforces a modular architecture heavily inspired by Angular, promoting DI, decorators, and a clear separation of concerns out-of-the-box.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify is unopinionated, providing a core of routing and middleware, allowing developers to structure their applications with minimal constraints.

differences.title: 2. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: NestJS performance is solid, but the abstraction layers can add overhead. It's optimized for developer experience over raw speed.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify prioritizes performance with a highly optimized engine, leveraging async hooks and avoiding unnecessary overhead for maximum throughput.

differences.title: 3. TYPING SYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: NestJS is built with TypeScript and heavily leverages its features, offering excellent type safety and developer tooling out of the box.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify supports TypeScript but is fundamentally JavaScript. Type safety relies on developer discipline or external TS integration.

differences.title: 4. ECOSYSTEM & PLUGINS
differences.leftDesc: NestJS has a rich ecosystem of official modules for common tasks like ORMs, GraphQL, WebSockets, and authentication, simplifying integration.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify has a vast plugin ecosystem, but integration might require more manual configuration compared to NestJS's built-in solutions.

differences.title: 5. LEARNING CURVE
differences.leftDesc: NestJS's comprehensive features and opinionated structure require a steeper learning curve, especially for those new to Angular concepts.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify's minimalist approach and focus on core web concepts make it generally easier to pick up for developers familiar with Node.js.

differences.title: 6. TESTABILITY
differences.leftDesc: NestJS provides excellent built-in testing utilities, including a testing module that simplifies unit and e2e testing of application logic.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify's testing approach is more conventional, relying on standard Node.js testing libraries and its request/response mocking capabilities.

differences.title: 7. DEVELOPMENT STYLE
differences.leftDesc: NestJS uses decorators and dependency injection for a declarative style, focusing on defining *what* needs to be done.
differences.rightDesc: Fastify's style is more imperative, emphasizing explicit control flow and middleware composition for defining *how* requests are handled.
